sec: HBV structure, genome figure, gene table, progression, infectivity, genotypes, pregnancy 90/10

items.q: Fill up (Structure): HBV is a DNA ______ virus; its genome is partially double stranded, ______ circular dsDNA.
items.exp: 'DNA : Hepadnavirus. Partially double stranded : Relaxed circular dsDNA.' Figure caption: 'Relaxed circular dsDNA'. (Book p1036)

items.q: Match — 1) Incomplete (+) strand 2) Complete (−) strand … A) Reverse transcriptase / polymerase B) Primer
items.exp: 'Incomplete (+) strand : primer; Complete (−) strand : Reverse transcriptase / polymerase.' (Book p1036)

items.q: Infective virion size and name, number of genotypes, and number of ORFs — as printed?
items.exp: 'Infective particle (virion) : 42 nm Dane particle; 10 genotypes in HBV; 4 open reading frames (ORFs)'. (Book p1036)

items.q: Which ORF label does NOT appear in the circular genome figure?
items.exp: Figure labels: ORF Pre S1, ORF Pre S2, HBsAg gene, ORF S, ORF P, Polymerase gene, ORF X, ORF Core, Pre C. There is no separate 'ORF E'. (Book p1036)

items.q: Gene table — match — 1) S-gene 2) C-gene 3) Pre C-gene … A) HBeAg, qualitative marker of infectivity & replication B) HBsAg, surface protein C) HBcAg, core protein (intracellular; anti-HBcAg in blood)
items.exp: S-gene → HBsAg surface protein; C-gene → HBcAg core protein (intracellular; anti-HBcAg in blood); Pre C-gene (part of C-gene) → HBeAg qualitative marker of infectivity & replication. (Book p1036)

items.q: Gene table continued — match — 1) P-gene 2) X-gene … A) HBx Ag, associated with hepatocellular carcinoma B) Polymerase, reverse transcriptase enzyme
items.exp: P-gene → polymerase / reverse transcriptase enzyme; X-gene → HBx Ag associated with HCC. (Book p1036)

items.q: Judge from the table: I HBcAg is intracellular and only its antibody is detected in blood. II HBeAg is a quantitative marker of replication.
items.exp: 'Core protein (Intracellular anti-HBcAg : in blood)'; HBeAg is the 'Qualitative marker of infectivity & replication' (HBV DNA is the quantitative marker, p1037). (Book p1036)

items.q: Progression diagram: incubation period, and the outcome percentages after acute hepatitis?
items.exp: 'Virus entry —60 days Incubation Period (IP)→ Acute hepatitis → 95–99% Recovery / 1–5% Chronic hepatitis'. (Book p1036)

items.q: Fill up: In the progression diagram, chronic hepatitis follows ______ transmission in ______%.
items.exp: '95% Vertical transmission' arrow into Chronic hepatitis. (Book p1036)

items.q: Which is NOT one of the three end-points drawn from cirrhosis in the progression diagram?
items.exp: Cirrhosis → Portal hypertension; Hepatocellular carcinoma; Liver failure. Notes: 'Also seen: NASH' (direct HCC arrow) and 'No treatment available.' (Book p1036)

items.q: Infectivity of HBV relative to HIV and HCV, as printed?
Genotype notes — match — 1) HAV 2) HEV 3) HBV commonest genotype 4) HBV HCC-risk genotype … A) 4 genotypes B) Genotype C C) 1 genotype D) Genotype A
items.exp: '1 genotype in HAV, 4 in HEV → Commonest : Genotype A; HCC risk : Genotype C'. (Book p1036)

items.q: HBV is 'found in all body fluids except ______'.
items.exp: 'Found in all body fluids except stools.' (Book p1036)

items.q: A pregnant woman is HBsAg-positive. Applying the printed 90/10 rule, what determines whether transmission risk is 90% or 10%?
items.exp: 'Pregnancy : 90/10 rule — HBsAg +ve + HBeAg +ve : 90% chance of transmission; HBeAg −ve : 10% chance.' (Book p1036)
